svg.title: Service stopped is not clock settled: three WSL2 situations from t = 0
svg.desc: Three side-by-side panels share one 0 to 120 second axis and one symmetric-log ppm scale with the historical plus or minus 1000 ppm screen. Left, Ubuntu 24.04 with systemd-timesyncd enabled: a documented default with two writers, Hyper-V implicit sync and timesyncd; no measured rate trace exists in this repository, so the panel shows an architecture-risk band only, plus the observation that four REALTIME steps of about +0.59 to +0.63 s occurred while the service was active in C1 phase A0. Middle, Ubuntu 24.04 after the timesyncd stop, the measured D4R2 series against Windows QPC: t = 0 is the window opening about 60 s after the confirmed stop with the unit still enabled; the PRE snapshot showed tick 10833 and freq 2157314; window 1 measured +26,665.299 to +26,724.999 ppm, outside the screen, about +0.80 s gained; windows 2 to 4 were -27.234 to +30.394, -32.612 to +25.100 and -27.169 to +32.177 ppm, each inside the screen and containing zero; the 120 s run was +6,661.607 to +6,676.217 ppm, still outside; the later POST snapshot showed tick 10000 and freq about -0.415 ppm; who set or reset tick is not established. Right, Ubuntu 26.04 fresh default: one default writer because chrony runs with -x and reads only; the project's bounded 300 s guest-side screen of MONOTONIC against MONOTONIC_RAW had all ten 30 s windows inside the screen, a full-run enclosure of -0.50 to -0.46 ppm and a worst window bound of -1.19 ppm; per-window values were not published. Summaries pop up as each 30 s window closes; running means in the middle panel are derived from the published windows. Motion is playback at ten times real time; with animation off the complete result is shown.
svg.text: Service stopped ≠ clock settled: three WSL2 situations from t = 0
How to read: the three panels share one 0–120 s axis and one ppm scale; the cursors move together at 10× real time.
Only the middle panel is a measured time series (D4R2). Left: architecture risk, no measured trace.
Right: bounded 300 s guest-side screen, different reference. Summaries pop up as each 30 s window closes.

g.text: nothing was measured in this state
two default writers can steer it
measure before you trust a window
→ do not assume a clean start state
t = 0 ≈ 60 s after the confirmed stop
* running means are derived from the published window enclosures, assuming equal 30 s windows; the 120 s run is the measured enclosure.
Upstream defaults (Microsoft, Canonical) combined with bounded project observations.
Different references, machines and durations; not a controlled comparison. 26.04 is not shown to fix WSL timing.
Who set tick 10833 or what reset it: not established. The controlled C1 test remained INCONCLUSIVE.
